# Chapter 22 - sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Asset and risk: Members' health data - special-category - at risk of
exposure through an uncontrolled shared file on unmanaged devices. Assessment:
High impact (sensitive data, GDPR, member trust), likely (broad access, personal
laptops, no control). Control: Move the data to an access-controlled system with
per-role rights and MFA (A.5.15, A.8.5); retire the spreadsheet. Residual: Low
- authorised misuse remains; formally accepted by the owner with a review
date. Assurance: Quarterly access review plus a sampled check that no copies
persist outside the system. (2) (a) Shelf-ware - replace it with the short set
of Chapter 15 that people actually use, and retire the rest. (b) Security
theatre - spend the visible-control money on the risk: Lock the server room;
keep the camera if it still earns its place. (c) Tick-box compliance - the
certificate met the letter; run the joiner--mover--leaver control for real and
let the certificate follow. (3) The audit proves the standard was met on that
day - a snapshot, not a state; the standard is a floor set for everyone, while
FastGoods' specific risks - R1--R3 - are its own to manage; compliance and
security relate in one direction: Manage the real risks well and compliance
falls out as evidence; reverse the direction and you hold a certificate over an
open gap. (4) (a) Check-and-report firing into improve: Chapter 17's review
trigger reopens the acceptance, with data. (b) Understand-and-govern: Chapter
5's regime map is redrawn, obligations flow into the ISMS and the SoA. (c) Check
into improve: A Chapter 16 finding - major, given Chapter 12's stakes - with
a remediation row, an owner, a deadline, and a re-test; twice-skipped makes it a
candidate repeat finding, which is a governance signal, not a calendar slip. (5)
General: Security is governed by finding the real risks, deciding about them
proportionately, and being able to show - with records an auditor could test
- that the decisions are made and kept. FastGoods: A 25-person shop took three
named risks from discovery through treatment, acceptance and audit to watched
closure - proving the cycle scales down without losing its shape.
